text:
maria: Quick design review — we need to pick a validation pattern for Settings > Model config. Options on the table: inline error blocks, error tooltips on hover, or a summarized error list at the top with focus jump. Also want to decide the pattern for destructive actions (Delete model) — typed confirm vs checkbox + modal vs toast + undo. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/model-settings (see pages: Validation Patterns) sam: I prefer inline errors for short forms — immediate, contextual. But we must handle keyboard users: move focus to first invalid field and announce errors with aria-live. devon: Inline works for a few fields, but our model config can be long. For long forms a summary at the top that links down to fields avoids scrolling and is better for discoverability. lee: Agree with both — hybrid is good. Show inline messages for fields that are visible, but also surface a concise summary at the top for long pages. Implementation notes: use aria-invalid, aria-describedby, and focus-first-invalid. alex: Quick accessibility nit: required markers. Don't rely solely on color. Use an asterisk plus aria-required="true". For screen readers we should include the word "required" in the label where it matters (or a visually-hidden suffix). maria: Thought: required markers only add noise when most fields are optional. Maybe show explicit "Required" label for crucial fields (model name, endpoint) and an asterisk for the rest. sam: On error tooltips — they look tidy but have discoverability issues. Hover tooltips are terrible for keyboard and touch. If we use tooltips, ensure the message is duplicated in DOM and exposed via aria-describedby. lee: Example markup I propose: ```
Name is required
``` And for the summary: ```
2 errors — press Tab to go to first error
``` devon: That looks solid. Also prefer the summary to include anchors: "1) Name missing — jump to field" which sets focus when activated. alex: Destructive actions: typed-confirm is safest but creates friction. Maybe apply typed-confirm for production-critical deletes (models with traffic) and use modal+toast undo for less-critical artifacts (drafts, snapshots). maria: Agreed. We should gate the heavy pattern by permission/impact. Also copy: default confirm copy is too terse. Suggest: "This will permanently delete the model and all inference data. This action cannot be undone." then input box that says "Type DELETE to confirm" for owner-level deletes. sam: Accessibility for modals: when modal opens, focus the typed input, trap focus, and ensure screen reader announces purpose: e.g.,
. Also ensure keyboard-only users can cancel the dialog easily. devon: For lower-friction deletes, a modal with a single checkbox "I understand this is permanent" + primary danger button + immediate toast with Undo (6s) feels friendlier. lee: One more thing — error animations. Avoid instant flashing — use subtle transitions. For screen readers, role="alert" is enough; avoid aria-live spam for each character change. alex: Copy tweaks per microcopy audit: replace "Are you sure?" with descriptive line. Example: "Delete model 'foo' — this will remove model, versions, and logs. Type DELETE to confirm." Also change primary button label from "Delete" to "Permanently delete model" for clarity. qa-bot: Reminder: QA test matrix: keyboard nav, NVDA, VoiceOver, iOS VoiceOver, Android TalkBack, mobile touch for tooltips. Also test autosave + validation interplay. maria: Decision summary: (1) Use inline errors for visible fields + top summary for long pages with focus-jump. (2) Use asterisk + aria-required, add visible "Required" where important. (3) Avoid hover-only tooltips; if used, duplicate in DOM with aria-describedby. (4) Destructive actions: use typed-confirm for high-impact owner-only deletes; use checkbox+modal+undo for others. (5) Update copy to be explicit and test with screen readers. Action items: design to update Figma (maria), engineering to implement aria attributes & focus behavior (lee/sam), QA to run matrix (devon). I'll update the design file and ping y'all when ready. :thumbsup:
